name: ESP32-S2

strapping.0: Chip boot mode (with GPIO46). Default weak pull-up (1). GPIO0=1 -> SPI boot; GPIO0=0 and GPIO46=0 -> Joint Download Boot (USB-OTG / UART / SPI download).
strapping.45: VDD_SPI (flash/PSRAM supply) voltage. Default weak pull-down (0) -> 3.3 V from VDD3P3_RTC via RSPI; 1 -> 1.8 V Flash Voltage Regulator. Ignored if eFuse EFUSE_VDD_SPI_FORCE=1 (then EFUSE_VDD_SPI_TIEH decides).
strapping.46: Chip boot mode (must be 0 with GPIO0=0 for download boot) and ROM message printing control (with EFUSE_UART_PRINT_CONTROL). Default weak pull-down (0). Input-only pin.

psram.condition: GPIO26 = SPICS1 = PSRAM CE# (in-package PSRAM on ESP32-S2R2 / ESP32-S2FN4R2, or recommended for off-package PSRAM). PSRAM also shares SPICLK/SPID/SPIQ/SPIWP/SPIHD (GPIO27,28,30,31,32) with flash. In 8-line (octal) SPI mode GPIO33-37 are additionally used (DQ4-DQ7, DQS/DM). ESP-IDF GPIO page: 'GPIO26-32 are usually used for SPI flash and PSRAM and not recommended for other uses.'

usb_jtag.note: USB OTG (full-speed) only: GPIO19 = USB_D-, GPIO20 = USB_D+ (internal PHY). Datasheet: 'by default, connected to the USB OTG. To function as GPIOs, these pins need to be reconfigured.' D-/D+ can be swapped via EFUSE_USB_EXCHG_PINS. The ESP32-S2 datasheet lists USB OTG but no USB-Serial-JTAG controller.

adc2_wifi_conflict: ADC2 is also used by Wi-Fi. adc_oneshot_read() has provided protection between the Wi-Fi driver and ADC oneshot mode driver. [ADC oneshot page]  |  ADC2 is also used by Wi-Fi. adc_continuous_start() has provided the protection between Wi-Fi driver and ADC continuous mode driver. [ADC continuous page]
notes: JTAG mapping (datasheet IO MUX table): MTCK=GPIO39, MTDO=GPIO40, MTDI=GPIO41, MTMS=GPIO42.

Flash pin mapping (datasheet Table 2-14 + IO MUX): GPIO26=SPICS1 (PSRAM CE#), GPIO27=SPIHD, GPIO28=SPIWP, GPIO29=SPICS0 (flash CS#), GPIO30=SPICLK, GPIO31=SPIQ, GPIO32=SPID. flash_spi lists 27-32; GPIO26 is the PSRAM chip-select. ESP-IDF GPIO page treats all of GPIO26-32 as SPI0/1 not recommended for other uses, and datasheet assigns all of GPIO26-32 Priority 4 ('already allocated or not recommended').
GPIO33-37 are the upper data lines and DQS of SPI0/1 in 8-line SPI mode; usable as GPIO only if flash/PSRAM is not in 8-line mode (datasheet 2.3.6).

GPIO46 is input-only. ESP-IDF GPIO page: 'GPIO46 is fixed to pull-down and is input only.' It is NOT listed in no_internal_pull because it does have a (fixed) pull-down; software pull-up is not available on it. An audit should flag any attempt to enable a pull-up or output on GPIO46.
ESP-IDF GPIO page notes: Strapping GPIO0, 45, 46; SPI0/1 GPIO26-32; JTAG GPIO39-42; GPI GPIO46. The GPIO page does not annotate UART0 or USB pins; those come from the datasheet.
Strapping hold time tH min 3 ms after CHIP_PU goes high (datasheet Table 3-2).
ADC continuous mode on ESP32-S2 uses SPI3 as DMA FIFO (adc_continuous page).
toolchain_prefix confirmed from ESP-IDF docs: xtensa-esp32s2-elf-gdb and xtensa-esp32s2-elf-addr2line. Installer package is xtensa-esp-elf.
sources: https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s2_datasheet_en.pdf (v1.9: Table 1-1, IO MUX table, Table 2-7, Sections 2.3.5/2.3.6, Table 2-14, Section 3 Boot Configurations)
